title: Andréa fait sa proposition  (Andréa Makes Her Pitch)

segments.t: Inside Hicham's luxury car on the French countryside highway, Andréa and her former classmate reconnect. Hicham sees through her casual ride request, forcing Andréa to reveal what she is really after: a wealthy savior for ASK. Listen to their dialogue in French first.
C'est drôle de se retrouver comme ça.
C'est peut-être un signe.
Personne n'attendait grand-chose de nous au lycée.
On s'en est quand même bien sortis.
Pourquoi tu es montée dans la voiture?
Quand on est riche, on apprend à reconnaître l'intérêt personnel.
C'est vrai, j'avais quelque chose en tête.
Mais je dois m'assurer que je peux te faire confiance.
On était au lycée ensemble. À cet âge-là, on ne ment pas.
Tu t'en souviens?
Oui, premier chagrin d'amour!
Je voulais montrer que je ne serais jamais comme eux.
Donc on est un peu pareils.
La vérité, c'est que mon agence... C'est une belle boîte. Un joyau, envié de tous.
Le patron est mort l'hiver dernier, depuis, le joyau est à vendre.
On ne veut pas être achetés, mais épousés.
On y est.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and understand Andréa's strategy.

'It is funny to meet again like this.' Andréa breaks the ice as they drive. Andréa opens with the word for 'funny' and lands on 'to meet again' at the close.
C'est peut-être un signe.
'Maybe it is a sign.' Hicham replies with an amused tone. A concise spoken phrase built around the French noun for 'sign'.
Personne n'attendait grand-chose de nous au lycée.
'Nobody expected much of us in high school.' She looks back on their awkward adolescence. Andréa pairs the verb meaning 'expected' with the noun for 'high school'.
On s'en est quand même bien sortis.
'We still did pretty well.' Hicham proudly reflects on their unexpected success. Hicham opens with the word for 'are' and lands on 'managed' at the close.
Pourquoi tu es montée dans la voiture?
'Why did you get into the car?' He cuts through the small talk with a direct question. Because Andréa is a woman, the past participle takes a silent extra e.
Quand on est riche, on apprend à reconnaître l'intérêt personnel.
'When you are rich, you learn to recognize self-interest.' Hicham shows he is no naive fool. Hicham pairs the verb meaning 'is' with the noun for 'the self-interest'.
C'est vrai, j'avais quelque chose en tête.
'It's true, I had something in mind.' Andréa admits that she has an ulterior motive. Notice how the verb for 'I had' leads straight into 'mind'.
Mais je dois m'assurer que je peux te faire confiance.
'But I must make sure that I can trust you.' She sets high terms before unveiling her plan. Andréa pairs the verb meaning 'must' with the noun for 'trust'.
On était au lycée ensemble. À cet âge-là, on ne ment pas.
'We were in high school together. At that age, one doesn't lie.' Hicham invokes their shared roots. Hicham opens with the word for 'were' and lands on 'lies' at the close.
Tu t'en souviens?
'Do you remember it?' Andréa tests his memory of their wild high-school parties. The verb meaning 'remember' anchors the whole remark.
Oui, premier chagrin d'amour!
'Yes, first heartbreak!' Hicham laughs about their youthful romantic disasters. A concise spoken phrase built around the French noun for 'heartbreak'.
Je voulais montrer que je ne serais jamais comme eux.
'I wanted to show that I would never be like them.' He explains his rebellious outsider spirit. Listen for the expression meaning 'wanted', which leads naturally into 'never'.
Donc on est un peu pareils.
'So we are kind of the same.' Andréa establishes their deep emotional affinity. The adverb meaning 'so' sharpens the verb for 'are' here.
La vérité, c'est que mon agence... C'est une belle boîte. Un joyau, envié de tous.
'The truth is that my agency... It's a great company. A jewel, envied by all.' She begins her pitch. Andréa opens with the word for 'truth' and lands on 'envied' at the close.
Le patron est mort l'hiver dernier, depuis, le joyau est à vendre.
'The owner died last winter, since then, the jewel has been for sale.' She explains the agency's crisis. Andréa opens with the word for 'boss' and lands on 'sale' at the close.
On ne veut pas être achetés, mais épousés.
'We don't want someone to buy us, but to marry us.' She delivers her brilliant closing metaphor. Listen for the expression meaning 'want', which leads naturally into 'married'.
On y est.

'We're here.' Hicham pulls the car to a halt right as she finishes her pitch. Hicham opens with the word for 'are' and lands on 'are' at the close. Now let's listen to Andréa's pitch once again from beginning to end.
